title: ACL Landmark Studies

positions.as_written: Read the method before the number on every one of these studies, because the method sets what the number can be used for.
Read the sectioning studies for attribution and the robotic studies for magnitude, and do not mix the two.
Read the in vivo strain work before giving a rehabilitation protocol, because the protocol is where that evidence actually applies.
Treat any single figure for ACL failure load as meaningless without the specimen age and the loading rate beside it.
Expect the rotational control question to stay open, and read new work on it for the control condition rather than for the conclusion.
Factor in the patient's age and physiology, since the failure load work says the ligament being matched is not the same ligament at twenty and at fifty.
Factor in comorbidities that change healing and rehabilitation tolerance.
Factor in the demands they place on the knee, because a pivoting athlete and a cyclist are asking different things of the same construct.
Factor in their psychological state, since fear of reinjury predicts return to sport more strongly than laxity does.
Weigh those together rather than applying the laboratory finding directly, and record which way the balance fell and why.
Read the contested literature for its control group, because the rotational control question has been answered differently by studies whose difference is in the comparator rather than in the finding.
